propositions: Reconciler core modules pass transport/client parameters without type annotations or annotate them as Any, preventing mypy from enforcing port protocol completeness and allowing methods to be called on untyped receivers without compile-time detection.

Absolute imports from rebar_reconciler.* package are unresolvable at type-check time due to runtime sys.path injection, causing mypy to widen annotations to Any even when formally typed, creating silent enforcement failures indistinguishable from bare annotations.

Relative imports within reconciler modules restore mypy's ability to resolve TicketTransport and enforce attribute access checks, provided the annotation itself is written with a resolvable import path, making import form a load-bearing requirement alongside annotation.

Four capability members (add_comment, set_relationship, get_comment_map, get_issuelinks_map) are carried as metaclass attributes for runtime hasattr checks but are not visible to mypy's Protocol attribute collection, causing false negatives in the existing AST audit that mypy can detect.

_TransportPortMeta metaclass is exonerated as a blocker; it remains load-bearing for uncached isinstance checks in the runtime conformance guard and does not interfere with static type checking when import paths are resolvable.
